data.title: Mechanical Pencil
data.solution:
# Get the length of the pencil's lead after executing all steps.
width = int(input())
lead = int(input())
n = int(input())
for i in range(n):
  command = input()
  if command == "PRESS":
    lead += 1
  elif command == "CLOSE":
    lead = 0
  else:
    lead -= int(command.split()[1])
    if lead < 0:
      lead = 0

# Print the pencil.
print(f'+{"-" * (width - 3)}\\')
print(f'|{" " * (width - 2)}|{"-" * lead}')
print(f'+{"-" * (width - 3)}/')
data.statement:
Output a mechanical pencil after executing all [[n]] steps of [[command]]. The length of the pencil's lead starts at [[lead]], and [[width]] represents the width of the pencil without its lead.

<<Commands:>>
{{PRESS}} - Increases the length of the pencil's lead by {{1}}.
{{CLOSE}} - Sets the lead's length to {{0}}.
{{PUSH}} always followed by <<the push power>>, separated by a space - Decreases the length of the pencil's lead by <<the push power>>.

<<How to Draw the Pencil:>> (recommended to check the example output if still confused)
<<Line 1:>> A {{+}} followed by ([[width]] - {{3}}) {{-}}'s, then followed by a backslash {{\}}.
<<Line 2:>> A {{|}} followed by ([[width]] - {{2}}) spaces followed by another {{|}}, then followed by trailing {{-}}'s of the length of the pencil after executing all [[n]] commands.
<<Line 3:>> A {{+}} followed by ([[width]] - {{3}}) {{-}}'s, then followed by a forward slash {{/}}.

<<Note:>> The lead's length never goes below {{0}}. If you get a {{PUSH}} command whose push power is greater than the lead's current length, then just treat it like a {{CLOSE}} command.

Good luck! ;)

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Output a mechanical pencil after executing all n steps of command. The length of the pencil's lead starts at lead, and width represents the width of the pencil without its lead.

Commands:
PRESS - Increases the length of the pencil's lead by 1.
CLOSE - Sets the lead's length to 0.
PUSH always followed by the push power, separated by a space - Decreases the length of the pencil's lead by the push power.

How to Draw the Pencil: (recommended to check the example output if still confused)
Line 1: A + followed by (width - 3) -'s, then followed by a backslash \.
Line 2: A | followed by (width - 2) spaces followed by another |, then followed by trailing -'s of the length of the pencil after executing all n commands.
Line 3: A + followed by (width - 3) -'s, then followed by a forward slash /.

Note: The lead's length never goes below 0. If you get a PUSH command whose push power is greater than the lead's current length, then just treat it like a CLOSE command.

Good luck! ;)
Input
Line 1: An integer width representing the width of the mechanical pencil without its led.
Line 2: An integer led representing the starting length of the mechanical pencil's led.
Line 3: An integer n representing the number of commands.
Next n lines: A string command representing the command to execute. Either PRESS, CLOSE, or PUSH followed by an integer push power. PUSH and push power are separated by a space.
Output
Lines 1-3: The mechanical pencil after following the steps in the statement.

Checklist:
* For the original Pair 5, please revise both cases to include all three commands and PUSH scenarios (a) and (b), with n close or equal to its upper bound of 15.
Constraints
3 ≤ width ≤ 20
0 ≤ lead ≤ 20
1 ≤ n ≤ 15
command is only the options listed in the statement.
1 ≤ push power ≤ 10
The final lead length is never less than 0.
Example
Input
5
0
3
PRESS
PRESS
PRESS
Output
+--\
|   |---
+--/
